HTTP 418 is **"I'm a teapot."**

It originates from the April Fools' joke RFC 2324 (Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol, 1998), which specified that any attempt to brew coffee with a teapot should return this error. RFC 7168 later extended it to teapots handling the `BREW` method.

It was never intended as a real status code, but it stuck around as an in-joke and is now implemented in many web frameworks and libraries. Some sites use it as a playful response for blocked or automated requests.
